races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Rated Race

runners_data.name: La Tache
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 5f on Good ground for G M Lyons under Colin Keane — the step back to five furlongs suits and her sim-going record of three from three is the standout positive; a prominent racer with a clean profile for this surface and trip.

runners_data.name: Star Prospect
runners_data.note: OR-120 colt for Joseph O'Brien who broke his maiden at 5f on Soft — Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride and he is the sole confirmed front-runner, meaning he can control this from the front without a fight; 34 days between runs is worth noting but his class advantage is clear.

runners_data.name: Grayrobin
runners_data.note: Won on debut at 5f on Good for trainer McGivern and runs off 120 — Chris Hayes takes over and the sim-going strike rate of one win from two runs is solid; a prominent racer whose winning form at this trip on this surface type makes him an obvious candidate to chase Star Prospect home.

runners_data.name: Sirocco Sands
runners_data.note: Dual winner whose latest success came over 6f on Good — a horse whose instinct is to race up with the pace but the density of prominent types in this field means he is unlikely to get to the front, which blunts his chance relative to what the form figures suggest.

runners_data.name: Lars Soldier
runners_data.note: Three wins at various tracks but none on Good ground — Wesley Joyce takes the 3lb claim and the horse has struggled in five recent outings to recapture his best; he naturally wants to race handily but will be squeezed for position with Star Prospect and Grayrobin ahead of him, and the going record here is thin.

runners_data.name: Belle Island
runners_data.note: Placed twice at five furlongs on Standard/AW surface for De Aguiar but her two runs on Good ground produced a sixth and a tenth — Wayne Lordan rides a genuine hold-up type whose going form here is a tangible concern, and she faces a race shape that is unlikely to generate enough pace for her to land a telling blow.

runners_data.name: Celestial Crown
runners_data.note: Jessica Maye takes the 7lb claim for JP Murtagh — a hold-up filly who has placed at 5f on Soft but posted an eighth and seventh on Good, and the combination of apprentice claim, unfavourable going record and a race shape that will not be run at a strong pace makes her prospects slim.

runners_data.name: Hi Corbett Court
runners_data.note: WJ Lee rides the 120-rated Twomey runner who has placed over 6f on Good but faces a drop to five furlongs — tongue-tie noted, and while he was a creditable third on debut over this longer trip, his hold-up style and the absence of strong early pace mean he has serious ground to make up in a very short straight.

races.paceDynamic: Star Prospect is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Dylan Browne McMonagle can dictate an unchallenged, metronomic gallop from the front on Good to Firm ground over five furlongs at Cork. Grayrobin and La Tache will press from prominent positions just off the pace, meaning the race is unlikely to be truly run at a dawdle, but Star Prospect should still control tempo on his own terms. Hi Corbett Court, Celestial Crown, and Belle Island are the designated hold-up runners but will face the challenge of closing on a well-rated front-runner who has not been pushed hard early. This field holds more prominent-leaning types than can realistically secure their natural position — Lars Soldier and Sirocco Sands are genuine front-runners redistributed to midfield, and in practice Star Prospect and likely Grayrobin will monopolise the front two berths, leaving those two to race in a compromised position. The race shape strongly favours horses comfortable racing prominently or just off a controlled lead, with the tactical premium sitting squarely on those who can travel close to Star Prospect and produce a clean turn of foot at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Star Prospect Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Star Prospect is allowed to dictate a comfortable tempo without any rival applying pressure to his outside.
scenarios.body: McMonagle settles Star Prospect in a smooth rhythm and the 120-rated colt simply picks up from two out, making the hold-up horses' task mathematically difficult on a flat five-furlong track. Horses who can race prominently just behind and quicken in the slip-stream are best placed, making Grayrobin and La Tache the natural beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Collar Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Star Prospect's early clip is quick enough to string out the field but leaves him vulnerable in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Grayrobin or La Tache, sitting a length or two off the pace and travelling well, hit the front as Star Prospect flattens inside the final furlong, with the Good to Firm ground suiting sharp two-year-olds who travel prominently. This is the scenario where a horse with a recent win at five furlongs on similar ground — La Tache's last-time-out win or Grayrobin's winning form — cashes in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Fliers Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong, compressing the field and setting up the track for a closing run from the rear.
scenarios.body: Hi Corbett Court or Celestial Crown would need the pace to be fast enough that they can reel in the leaders across the flat Cork straight, a scenario that demands more tempo than this race shape currently projects. Both are genuine hold-up types but face a structural disadvantage if Star Prospect settles into a controlled canter, and neither has shown the form ceiling to overcome that margin at this level.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Chaos Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for position between Lars Soldier, Sirocco Sands, and the front pair causes a compressed, scrambly gallop with no clear leader.
scenarios.body: With multiple prominent types squeezed into a tight early formation the race could degenerate into a sprint from the two-furlong mark with no horse having a positional advantage, slightly boosting the hold-up brigade's prospects. Belle Island and Celestial Crown are the beneficiaries in this unlikely scramble, but their below-par form figures on Good ground make this a low-conviction shape.

watchPoints.text: Star Prospect's reaction to a solo lead is the single biggest race-shaper — if McMonagle allows him to coast at a comfortable clip unchallenged, no hold-up horse in this field has the form ceiling to reel him in over a flat five furlongs.

Lars Soldier and Sirocco Sands are both natural front-runners who will instinctively try to press forward at the break — any early bump or crowding between stalls two through five could cause interference that disrupts Grayrobin and La Tache's prominent positions.

Celestial Crown's 7lb claim from Jessica Maye is a substantial riding allowance, but the filly's Good-ground figures (8th, 7th) suggest the surface itself is the primary concern rather than weight, so the claim should not significantly inflate her chance in the market.

Hi Corbett Court drops from 6f to 5f for the first time in a race wearing a tongue-tie — Twomey runners can improve sharply with gear changes but the trip reduction for a hold-up horse in a pace-controlled race is a compounding structural disadvantage worth monitoring.

La Tache runs for the third time in the last five days at an age of just two — the quick turnaround for a juvenile on Good to Firm ground is worth flagging, though Lyons and Keane clearly hold the filly in high regard to pitch her in again this quickly.

races.name: Doneraile Handicap

runners_data.name: Kendall Roy
runners_data.note: Won last two outings over 5f at Cork on good ground with Chris Hayes, and is the only confirmed front-runner in the field — small trainer yard (0/2 past 14 days) is the main knock, but the horse's form figures here are outstanding and he is in his ideal race shape.

runners_data.name: Sarahmae
runners_data.note: Back just two days after a recent run — Denis Hogan is a high-volume operator and clearly happy to run her again quickly — has won twice at 5f on good and brings a light 136lbs; a genuine prominent type who should get a clean position just off Kendall Roy.

runners_data.name: Erosandpsyche
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up specialist (style authentic, not redistributed) who has placed six times in similar conditions — visors and tongue-tie noted, suggesting the yard is coaxing out every ounce; consistent at 5f on good ground but his finishing kick rarely brings him closer than third at this level.

runners_data.name: Howd'yadoit
runners_data.note: Three-year-old trained by G M Lyons whose yard is firing at 7/31 over the past fortnight — won over this trip on good ground last time and should travel comfortably prominent; the 5lb claimer Nicola Burns is a slight concern but the horse's recent form speaks for itself.

runners_data.name: Chicago Call
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh runner returning after 68 days off — longest absence in the field — and is a hold-up type stepping back to 5f having raced over 6f-7f recently; the layoff and the drop in trip are both flags, though he has placed on good ground before.

runners_data.name: Eclairage
runners_data.note: Terry Casey's 7lb claim is an asset but this horse's natural prominent style cannot be fully expressed — pushed to a midfield map position by the numerical weight of pace in this field — and a record of just three places from 15 similar-going runs suggests consistency issues regardless of where he settles.

runners_data.name: Rosie Frith
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for Patrick Magee (4/14 past 14 days) on a filly who has won twice at 5f — once on good, once on standard — and whose recent form string (1-8014) shows good days and bad; a genuine prominent type who should get a reasonable berth and will be ridden positively by Keane.

runners_data.name: Ipanema Queen
runners_data.note: Front-running tendency means she is one of several prominent horses who will not find her natural position at the head of affairs here, pushing her further back than ideal; Robson De Aguiar yard is in modest form (2/16) and this three-year-old's last three runs over 5f on good ground show three finishes of 8th, 6th, and 4th — not uncompetitive but lacking a decisive blow.

runners_data.name: Genesis
runners_data.note: Michael Mulvany yard is active (3/12) and Genesis has won twice at 5f on good ground with strong similar-going statistics (13/15 runs on comparable surfaces) — naturally prominent but squeezed into a midfield map slot by the weight of pace in this race; Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim preserves his chance if he gets a cleaner run than the map suggests.

runners_data.name: Allsortz
runners_data.note: Luke McAteer rides this David Marnane three-year-old who won at 5f on soft and placed at 6f on good — a hold-up type returning after 27 days, which is not unusual; no obvious going concern, but a career high-OR appearance here suggests the handicapper may have caught up with him.

runners_data.name: Fox In Flight
runners_data.note: Rebecca Parsons takes the 10lb claim for Marnane, and Fox In Flight has shown a 2nd at 5f on good ground in her history — however, she is a natural prominent runner who cannot get her preferred early position in this field, and her four most recent finishes (5th, 9th, 2nd, 12th) show a volatile profile that makes her difficult to rely upon.

races.paceDynamic: Kendall Roy is the one confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 5f sprint on good-to-firm ground at Cork, and with no serious rival to force a genuine pace battle, he is expected to dictate from the gates and control the tempo at a sustainable clip. The going report confirms good-to-firm conditions throughout the card, which will reward horses who travel efficiently and maintain their momentum rather than those who need a strong pace to deliver a late surge. Several horses — Eclairage, Ipanema Queen, Genesis, and Fox In Flight — are natural prominent types who will be seeking to race close to the pace, but with Kendall Roy firmly established in front and only so many positions available in the first two to three lengths, those redistributed runners will be squeezed into tighter berths than their natural style demands, creating a congested early phase. This shape strongly favours genuine hold-up horses who can benefit from any mid-race crowding and closers who possess a sharp turn of foot on fast ground — but more directly, it rewards the horse who secures an uncontested lead (Kendall Roy) or the one prominent type who slots cleanly into second position and travels powerfully throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kendall Roy Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Kendall Roy jumps well and establishes an uncontested lead within the first furlong, dictating a fair-but-not-suicidal pace on fast ground.
scenarios.body: Settling cleanly in front on good-to-firm Cork turf, Kendall Roy uses his proven course-and-distance form (1/5f/GOO most recent) to keep a measured gallop that rewards his stamina and punishes those forced to race in unnatural positions; with no genuine rival to seriously challenge him early, he hits the rising ground in the closing stages with reserves intact.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Poacher Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent types — most likely Sarahmae or Howd'yadoit — travels smoothly in second or third and quickens past a tying Kendall Roy inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Sarahmae brings sharp recent form (wins at 5f on good ground) and a low weight, while Howd'yadoit has the class and trainer form (G M Lyons, 7/31 past 14 days) to take advantage if Kendall Roy pays for any early exertion; on good-to-firm ground the horse travelling most fluently into the final 100 yards is rewarded.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a finish for closers — more likely if the several prominent types crowd the early stages and lift the tempo.
scenarios.body: Erosandpsyche has strong hold-up credentials and decent placing form over this course and distance, while Chicago Call has the profile of a horse who appreciates a strong pace; fast ground suits both, and any fractional increase in early pace caused by prominent runners jostling for position could open a late lane.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Midfield Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the prominence scramble causes interference early, slowing the effective pace and creating a stop-start tempo that catches the field flat.
scenarios.body: Rosie Frith and Allsortz, both with genuine finishing kicks at 5f on good ground, could pick up the pieces if the race turns messy; this scenario requires significant crowding from the redistributed horses (Eclairage, Fox In Flight, Ipanema Queen) forcing an uneven gallop, which is plausible but the least likely outcome given Kendall Roy's anticipated clean break.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a crowded break from the gates — Eclairage, Ipanema Queen, Genesis, and Fox In Flight will all be seeking prominent berths that do not all exist, and any jostling in the first furlong could hamper multiple runners including Rosie Frith.

Kendall Roy's recent form over 5f at Cork on good ground is excellent, but Chris Hayes will need a clean jump — if he is slow out of the stalls, the prominent scramble behind him could sweep past him before he re-establishes.

Chicago Call is returning from 68 days off for JP Murtagh — the hold-up style means he needs things to go right late, and the short 5f trip on fast ground with no recent run is a combination that needs monitoring in the market.

The going report lists every race on the card as Good to Firm — conditions are fast and consistent, which historically at Cork rewards horses on the pace or those with a high cruising speed rather than deep closers; Erosandpsyche's profile is authentic but fast ground late-season at this track can blunt his finishing effort.
Trainer Marnane has two runners (Allsortz and Fox In Flight) — watch for any market drift or support that might indicate stable preference, as both are unlikely to benefit from the same scenario.

runners_data.name: Heart Of Eternity
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a fading-finish flag and poor recent form (068000), returning after 15 days under Denis Hogan; only 4 similar-going runs from 9 yield no wins and two places, suggesting the pace shape here does not suit.

runners_data.name: I'm Spartacus
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in this field; Adam Caffrey rides for Adrian McGuinness who has 3 wins from 32 over 14 days, and seven runs at this course-distance-going combination include one win — the uncontested lead is the key asset here, though the style-fit tag (0.93) notes it is officially mapped slightly out of role.

runners_data.name: Billboa
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse dropping back to 6f from 5f form on slower surfaces; W P Browne stable has just 0 wins from 1 run in 14 days and similar-going form of 2 runs from 15 yields no wins or places, making this a difficult profile to fancy.

runners_data.name: Rosato
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with three wins and three places from 15 similar-going runs — the best similar-going record among the prominent types; Charles Weld's yard is quiet (0/0 in 14 days) and a 42-day absence is a query, but the course form is solid.

runners_data.name: El Fontenaro
runners_data.note: Has placed four times from 15 similar-going runs and his two second-place finishes on identical ground this season show a consistent prominent-racing profile; Ronan Whelan is a strong booking and 13 days since last run is a normal turnaround.

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: Four places from 15 similar-going runs at 5-6f, prominent racer with a top jockey (Dylan Browne McMonagle) booked fresh off a 7-day turnaround; Batt Burke sends this horse out in good shape and the 6f Cork track on good-to-firm should be fine.

runners_data.name: Captain Ciano
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with a fading-finish flag, all recent form over 8-10f and now sharply dropped in trip; mapped to midfield here only because the rear is overloaded — the style-fit discount (0.91) and distance concern combine to make this a very speculative runner over 6f.

runners_data.name: Jazzit
runners_data.note: Horse-headgear-fitted hold-up type whose best form at 5f on good comes from a 3rd last time in similar going; the redistribution to midfield reflects the crowded hold-up group rather than its natural racing position, and the 30-day absence under a 7lb claimer (Sadhbh Tormey) adds risk.

runners_data.name: Platino Bianco
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with a tv headgear combination and one win from 15 similar-going runs over 5f — the win at 5f on good is relevant form; Robert Whearty rides and 21 days since last run is unremarkable.

runners_data.name: Jampa Ling
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with one place from 9 similar-going runs and a fading-finish flag; a 3-year-old trained by Kieran Cotter who has 0 wins from 3 over 14 days, returned 13 days ago — the tendency to fade undermines the prominent style here.

runners_data.name: Alandownunder
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type with a fading-finish flag and all form at 6f+ on good in the 8-9 range — no wins or places from 6 similar-going runs; the 24-day break and 5lb claimer (Nicola Burns) do not help the case.

runners_data.name: The Cosy Corner
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse with a fading-finish flag and a 0W0P record from 4 good-going runs, all finishing 9th or worse; Chris Hayes is a competent jockey but the form profile gives little encouragement in a 21-runner sprint.

runners_data.name: Dubai Opulence
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with fading-finish flag and only 2 runs from 5 similar-going starts yielding no wins or places; Colin Keane is an excellent jockey but the horse's form in 6f handicaps on good ground is thin and the 13-day turnaround is normal.

runners_data.name: Auguste Gusteau
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old true hold-up horse with all four runs finishing 6th-9th; Ben Coen's booking is a positive marker but the horse is mapped away from its natural position and its short four-run profile (0W0P from 4 similar-going runs) offers little hope.

runners_data.name: Love Bomb
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a fading-finish flag whose one win came over 5f on good for W McCreery; the redistribution away from its natural rearward berth is a significant style issue, and fading in finish in this pace shape makes it hard to recommend despite W J Lee in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Banter
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in the lower OR bracket (45) who has one place from 15 similar-going runs, mostly at 6f on good; Andrew Slattery has 4 wins from 39 over 14 days and a 7lb claimer (Jimmy Dalton) takes the ride — moderate profile.

runners_data.name: Hastily
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up horse with a fading-finish flag and a 42-day absence; all recent form is at 7f-16f on good and the redistribution away from the rear reflects the field's overcrowded hold-up group rather than any change in role — very weak similar-going record (1W2P from 15 runs).

runners_data.name: Snowballs
runners_data.note: Hold-up type (0W0P from 12 similar-going runs) who has finished in the 5th-9th range consistently; Leigh Roche rides and the 7-day turnaround is fine, but the redistribution note means this horse cannot execute its preferred style and form does not compensate.

runners_data.name: Ballerina Dancer
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse with only three runs (all finishing 9-14th) and a fading-finish flag; Luke McAteer rides after a 53-day break, the longest absence in the field, and the form profile at 7-8f on good offers nothing transferable to a 6f sprint.

runners_data.name: Niobite
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with three runs all finishing 12th-15th; trained by Patrick J Flynn with 1 win from 6 over 14 days and a 30-day gap — fading-finish flag and a redistribution out of natural position compound a very thin profile.

runners_data.name: You Smiled
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse with a headgear (t) flag and four runs all finishing 7th-11th; jockey-trainer combination (Andrew Slattery riding for himself, 4/39 in 14 days) is noted but the form and redistribution context make this a low-expectation runner.

races.paceDynamic: I'm Spartacus is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 21-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — this horse sets a sustainable, uncontested gallop over 6f on good-to-firm ground at Cork, which is an exceptionally favourable scenario for a confirmed pace-setter. The field is packed with hold-up types — Love Bomb, Jazzit, Captain Ciano, Auguste Gusteau, Hastily, Snowballs and others are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because they simply cannot all get to the rear in a 21-runner sprint; in reality, the field holds far more off-the-pace types than can execute their natural style, meaning the pace dynamic skews heavily toward the front. Prominent-racing types El Fontenaro, Whatswrongnow, Rosato and Sovereign Banter will track I'm Spartacus at a comfortable clip, and with no pressure on the leader the fractions will be steady rather than searching. The clear tactical verdict: this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or tracking the pace in the first half, as the lone front-runner dictates an honest but not brutal tempo and the field's abundance of hold-up types will be forced to make ground from further back than ideal on a flat, galloping track.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If I'm Spartacus bowls along uncontested and the steady pace is never truly tested by a rival.
scenarios.body: I'm Spartacus dictates throughout at a comfortable clip, the prominent trackers El Fontenaro and Whatswronwnow sit close enough to challenge but the leader has enough in hand to repel them; good-to-firm Cork turf rewards a horse that settles and travels well at the front. Horses with course-and-distance form at a sane pace benefit most, and I'm Spartacus's 1W from 7 runs at this course-distance-going combination underlines the profile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If I'm Spartacus fades in the final furlong and the two closest prominent trackers sprint past in a driving finish.
scenarios.body: El Fontenaro's four places from 15 similar-going runs and consistent 6f form at Cork marks him as the most likely beneficiary, while Whatswrongnow has four seconds from 15 comparable runs and a top jockey in Dylan Browne McMonagle; both travel prominently and are ideally placed when the pace eases in the final 100 yards. This scenario rewards horses with the ability to accelerate off a genuine gallop once the front-runner is spent.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and prominent horses tie up, allowing a well-placed midfield horse to pick them off late.
scenarios.body: Platino Bianco has a win from 15 similar-going runs and is a genuine hold-up type who has shown ability to finish from off the pace over 5-6f; Snowballs has been placed in similar fields and, if allowed to bowl along unimpeded at the rear, could deliver a late rattle. However, the bulk of the field's true closers have poor finishing records and several are redistibuted types, so this shape requires a specific collapse at the front that is not the base case.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Breaks Up Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of 21 causes early traffic incidents, bunching and interference that scrambles the expected positional order.
scenarios.body: In a 21-runner handicap sprint, a scrimmage off the gates could see several horses lose ground early and make the race unpredictable, but this scenario is rare on a flat, well-running Cork straight; any beneficiary would need tactical luck and ability to weave through. Captain Ciano and Jazzit, true hold-up types, could theoretically benefit if front-runners capitulate spectacularly, but their style-fit discounts and fading-finish flags make this a low-confidence shape.

watchPoints.text: I'm Spartacus must be tracked from the gates — if Adam Caffrey gets a clean break and settles on the lead uncontested, the entire race shape revolves around whether this horse can sustain the gallop to the line in a 21-runner field.

El Fontenaro and Whatswrongnow are the two most likely prominent horses to track the pace and challenge late — watch their early positions in the stalls draw; if either is squeezed out or loses a length at the start, their chance is materially reduced in a 6f handicap.

runners_data.name: Holy Lettuce

runners_data.name: Lady In The Gods

races.paceDynamic: Alphonsus Liguori is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field and should stride to the front unchallenged from the outset, setting a measured, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over a mile at Cork. With no genuine pace rival to press him, Dylan Browne McMonagle can dictate terms and control the tempo entirely on his own terms, making this a classic leader's race in structure. The three hold-up horses — Fate's Gambit, The Monday Club, and Lady In The Gods — will need to close ground that may never truly open up if the pace is kept honest but not punishing. This race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-lead profile: a horse who can travel close to Alphonsus Liguori or sit just off the bridle and pick up in the straight holds the decisive positional advantage, with pure closers facing the toughest task against an uncontested front-runner on fast ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Alphonsus Liguori is allowed to stride clear and set an uncontested gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Alphonsus Liguori dictates from the front without a rival willing or able to challenge his position, conserving enough energy to quicken in the straight on Good to Firm ground; his O'Brien stable send him here fresh off a win and his style fits perfectly with the race shape on offer.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Holy Lettuce Stalks, Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Holy Lettuce, lightly raced and unexposed, tracks the leader and produces a sharp turn of foot in the straight.
scenarios.body: Holy Lettuce's unknown ceiling as a lightly-raced three-year-old with a solid OR of 120 means she could simply outclass this field if she travels well in behind Alphonsus Liguori and quickens past at the furlong pole; W.J. Lee's judgement of pace from a prominent position makes this the most realistic counter to the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to set up a closing run and one of the hold-up types finds a clear run in the straight.
scenarios.body: The Monday Club or Fate's Gambit would need the tempo to be genuinely taxing to make up significant ground from off the pace on fast ground, which is unlikely given only one genuine front-runner; with closers mapped forward out of their natural positions, this scenario is further undermined by their inability to settle truly last.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Alphonsus Liguori is slow away or races too freely early, disrupting the expected pace structure entirely.
scenarios.body: A chaotic, falsely-run race with no clear leader would compress the field and turn it into a sprint finish from which any of the hold-up types at big odds could profit; Lady In The Gods would be the longest shot to benefit, though her finishing tendency to fade makes her an unreliable vehicle for this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Alphonsus Liguori — if McMonagle takes this horse to the front and controls the gallop from the outset, the field will have almost no mechanism to reel him in on Good to Firm ground over a mile with no pressing rival.

Holy Lettuce — lightly raced and entirely unexposed, she could be significantly ahead of her single run on the clock; watch how W.J. Lee positions her in the first two furlongs as a prominent pitch would make her the most dangerous threat.

Fate's Gambit — mapped to midfield but a genuine hold-up type in nature; if she attempts to race further back than her map position suggests, she may find herself with too much ground to make up in a slowly-run race.
The Monday Club — dropping from 10f to 1m having only run once; the trip reduction is an unknown that could spark improvement or expose a horse who simply needs further to be effective.|

races.name: Racing Again August 3rd Handicap

runners_data.name: Nathema
runners_data.note: 90-day absence is a significant concern; runs H style but has a sim-going record of just 1 effort at 3f+ on comparable ground, and the finishing-fade flag suggests she won't pick off the pace-setter without a truly honest gallop.

runners_data.name: Connecteo
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride and has placed twice on similar going in six attempts; the hold-up style means he'll need to make ground, but he's run 2nd over 12f on good ground and has the profile to track a honest pace without getting caught in traffic.

runners_data.name: Glen Echo
runners_data.note: Ran 3rd over 13f at Cork on good just 7 days ago, which is the most relevant piece of form in the race, but the fading flag and 0-from-5 on similar going are serious cautions; Cromwell's 7-day turnaround angle is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Point Cartwright
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner; has placed 3 times from 7 on good, handles the trip and course, and the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild concern — he's rated as racing slightly out of role — but as the only confirmed pacer here, his positional advantage offsets that.

runners_data.name: Guildhall Graduate
runners_data.note: Cromwell's second string; a genuine hold-up horse whose true nature is obscured by the midfield map placement — he has drifted to double-figures in finishes on this ground and needs a pace collapse that is unlikely to materialise.

runners_data.name: Millhone
runners_data.note: Charles Weld's yard shows 0 runs in 14 days, and the fading flag alongside a 0-from-5 sim-going record suggests this horse needs soft conditions to be competitive; 20 days off is fine fitness-wise but the going is all wrong.

runners_data.name: Amethyst Stone
runners_data.note: DBM takes the ride, which is the one positive, but Amethyst Stone has finished 6th, 9th, 12th, 6th and 15th in five attempts on good ground — a dire sim-going record — and the hold-up style displaced into midfield makes a forward move hard to construct.

runners_data.name: Tavarua
runners_data.note: The tongue-tie and blinkers combination suggests connections are trying something new, but six of his last nine finishes have been 8th or worse and his best 10f performance came on soft ground; W J Lee has to overcome a very modest profile here.

runners_data.name: Wingit
runners_data.note: Colin Keane is a major positive, and a 2nd at 13f on good is encouraging stamina evidence; the REDISTRIBUTED tag means Wingit won't settle as far back as the map suggests, but that could actually suit him if he slots into mid-division naturally.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: Style is listed as unknown (U), which gives Foley tactical freedom; recent form shows a 2nd and 4th on good ground at 10f, and he's the most interesting runner without a fixed positional label — connections could exploit the lone leader if they choose to track.

runners_data.name: Canon Law
runners_data.note: Brendan Duke's yard is quiet (0 from 4 in 14 days) and Canon Law has not won or placed beyond 7f on comparable ground; the hold-up style stuck in a congested midfield makes this a very difficult winner to construct.

runners_data.name: Kuma Queen
runners_data.note: Coming back after 339 days off, which is an enormous absence; three career runs all at 8f on good produced finishes of 7th, 10th and 10th — stepping dramatically up to 1m4f on a quick comeback looks a very big ask.

runners_data.name: Cadreville
runners_data.note: Finished 3rd over 10f on good ground 11 days ago, which is encouraging, and Jarlath Fahey's runner has shown improvement at staying trips; the hold-up style redistributed forward creates a positional mismatch, but this horse has arguably the best recent-run form among the closers.

races.paceDynamic: Point Cartwright is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 1m4f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Cork, and with no genuine rival to press him, he is set to control fractions from the front at a pace he dictates himself — a significant positional advantage at a trip that rewards those able to settle and quicken from the front. The field behind him is overwhelmingly stacked with hold-up types, but because there are far more closers than the race map can accommodate at the rear, Guildhall Graduate, Amethyst Stone, Wingit, Tavarua, Canon Law, Kuma Queen and Cadreville have all been redistributed forward on the map — in reality, many of these will end up bunched in mid-to-rear traffic, forced to cover ground late. Borora Aura (style unknown) and Connecteo represent the most flexible threats capable of sitting handy without being tagged as pure front-runners. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape — a single uncontested leader on a flat, fast-ground track — strongly favours either Point Cartwright continuing to the line unchallenged, or a horse sitting just behind him in the prominent-to-midfield tier who tracks the pace without expending energy in a battle for position; true hold-up horses face a traffic and ground-loss disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Point Cartwright Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Point Cartwright meets no early pressure and controls the gallop throughout at a sustainable tempo on fast ground.
scenarios.body: He dictates from the front, sets a fair but not suicidal pace over 1m4f on good-to-firm Cork, and arrives at the straight with a head of steam and rivals unable to quicken enough to reel him in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting just off Point Cartwright's pace in second or third conserves enough energy to collar him in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Connecteo's hold-up style and course form make him a candidate to sit close enough without fighting for position, while Borora Aura's flexible unknown style could see Shane Foley park him handy and pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If Point Cartwright burns himself out by setting a faster-than-expected gallop and the race develops into a stamina test in the straight.
scenarios.body: The redistribution means most genuine closers will be stuck mid-pack or wider, but Wingit (second at 13f) and Cadreville (third at 10f) have the staying profiles to benefit if the tempo truly honest-ifies the race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Ups Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Point Cartwright capitulates turning in and a wall of horses arrives simultaneously from deep.
scenarios.body: The redistributed hold-up brigade — Guildhall Graduate, Amethyst Stone, Kuma Queen — would need a career-best effort and a clear run, which the congested field makes unlikely, but a complete pace collapse is this scenario's only door.

watchPoints.text: Point Cartwright's early strides are critical — if Ronan Whelan sends him clear and no rival follows, the race is effectively over as a tactical contest by halfway.

Borora Aura's unknown style label means Shane Foley could place him anywhere in the field; watch the early position, as sitting second or third behind the lone front-runner would make him a significant danger.

Wingit's 4-day turnaround (LR:4d) is unusually short — Colin Keane may be under instructions to be conservative early, which could mean he ends up further back than his REDISTRIBUTED midfield slot suggests.
Kuma Queen's 339-day absence and sharp trip-up from 8f to 1m4f warrants monitoring — if she shows any early signs of distress or fails to settle, she could compromise the horses directly behind her.
Glen Echo ran at Cork just 7 days ago over 13f; watch whether the short turnaround shows in the final quarter-mile, as the fading flag twice in recent form suggests she may tire noticeably late.
